# reci

Compile declarative CI recipes into fully-wired GitHub Actions workflows with typed data-flow validation.

To install:	`pip install reci`

## Why reci

Writing GitHub Actions workflows by hand means wading through hundreds of lines of
boilerplate: forwarding step outputs to job outputs, threading `needs.X.outputs.Y`
expressions across jobs, and copy-pasting config values that belong in one place.
When something changes you touch a dozen lines across three jobs — and one typo
silently breaks your pipeline.

**reci** lets you write a short recipe that says *what* your CI does (which actions,
in what order, with what config), and the compiler handles *how* — auto-wiring
cross-job outputs, injecting config from `pyproject.toml`, and validating data-flow
before you push.

## Agent skills (recommended)

reci ships with CLI and Python APIs (see [below]()), but the best way to use it
is through **AI agent skills** — structured instructions that let coding assistants
operate reci on your behalf. Instead of memorizing CLI flags and YAML syntax, just
say what you want:

-  *“Set up CI for this project”*
-  *“Migrate my existing workflow to reci”*
-  *“What CI actions make sense here?”*

### Available skills

| Skill          | What it does                                                                       |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [ci-setup]()   | Examines your project, proposes a CI plan, writes a recipe, compiles to a workflow |
| [ci-migrate]() | Converts an existing GitHub Actions workflow into a reci recipe                    |
| [ci-advisor]() | Interactive discussion about what CI pipeline makes sense for your project         |
| [reci-dev]()   | Guide for contributors — architecture, adding rules, adding adapters               |

### Using the skills

The skills live in `reci/data/skills/`, so they ship inside `pip install reci` and any agent host can install them from the repo with the GitHub CLI (`gh` 2.90+):

```bash
gh skill install i2mint/reci ci-setup
gh skill install i2mint/reci ci-migrate
gh skill install i2mint/reci ci-advisor
```

**Claude Code** — symlink or copy the skills into your project or your personal skills directory (from a checkout, or from the installed package’s `reci/data/skills/`):

```bash
# Make available to all your projects
ln -s /path/to/reci/reci/data/skills/ci-setup ~/.claude/skills/ci-setup
ln -s /path/to/reci/reci/data/skills/ci-migrate ~/.claude/skills/ci-migrate
ln -s /path/to/reci/reci/data/skills/ci-advisor ~/.claude/skills/ci-advisor

# Or just for one project
ln -s /path/to/reci/reci/data/skills/ci-setup my-project/.claude/skills/ci-setup
```

Then invoke with `/ci-setup`, `/ci-migrate`, or `/ci-advisor` in Claude Code.
See the [Claude Code skills docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) for details.

**Other agents** — the skills are plain Markdown files following the open
[Agent Skills standard](https://agentskills.org). For Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf,
and other tools, see the standard’s
[integration guide](https://agentskills.org/integrations).

## Quick start

```python
from reci import (
    parse_recipe_string,
    compile_recipe,
    dump_workflow,
    ActionSpec,
    InputSpec,
    OutputSpec,
)

recipe = parse_recipe_string("""
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '${{ config.python_version }}'
      - id: run_tests
        run: pytest
""")

# Action specs can be fetched from GitHub or provided manually
specs = {
    "actions/checkout@v4": ActionSpec(ref="actions/checkout@v4"),
    "actions/setup-python@v5": ActionSpec(
        ref="actions/setup-python@v5",
        inputs={"python_version": InputSpec(name="python_version", default="3.x")},
    ),
}

config = {"python_version": "3.12"}
workflow = compile_recipe(recipe, specs, config=config)
print(dump_workflow(workflow))
```

The compiler:

- Injects a `setup` job that exports config values as job outputs
- Rewrites `${{ config.* }}` to `${{ needs.setup.outputs.* }}`
- Auto-wires `needs:` edges from data-flow dependencies
- Generates the cross-job output forwarding ceremony (step output -> job output -> `needs` consumption)

## CLI

```bash
# Inspect an action's input/output contract
reci inspect actions/setup-python@v5

# Compile a recipe to workflow YAML
reci compile recipe.yml --output .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Validate a recipe + config
reci validate --recipe recipe.yml --format cli

# Scaffold a config skeleton from a recipe
reci scaffold recipe.yml
```

## Five-level input resolution

For each action input, the compiler resolves its value using this precedence:

1. **Explicit `with:`** in the recipe — used verbatim
2. **Upstream output match** — `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.<name> }}`
3. **Config value** (scoped `action__key`, then shared `key`) — `${{ needs.setup.outputs.<key> }}`
4. **Default from action.yml** — omitted (GitHub uses the default)
5. **Required + no source** — validation error

## Validation

ESLint-style severity (`error`/`warning`/`info`) with ruff-style rule prefixes:

| Rule    | Category   | What it catches                                           |
|---------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| DAG001  | Structure  | Cycle detected                                            |
| DAG002  | Structure  | Duplicate output name in a job                            |
| FLOW001 | Data flow  | Required input has no source                              |
| FLOW002 | Data flow  | Ambiguous wiring (multiple upstream matches)              |
| FLOW006 | Data flow  | Matrix job output consumed downstream (non-deterministic) |
| CONF001 | Config     | Required config key missing                               |
| PURE001 | Purity     | `run:` step breaks typed contract                         |
| ACT002  | Action     | Referenced action not found                               |

## Config adapters

Read CI config from your project file of choice:

| Adapter        | Section          | Library              |
|----------------|------------------|----------------------|
| `pyproject`    | `[tool.ci]`      | tomlkit (round-trip) |
| `wads`         | `[tool.wads.ci]` | tomlkit              |
| `package-json` | `"ci"` key       | json                 |
| `yaml`         | `.ci.yml`        | ruamel.yaml          |

## The recipe format

A recipe looks like a GitHub Actions workflow with reci extensions:

- **`${{ config.* }}`** — references to config values (resolved from pyproject.toml etc.)
- **`bind:`** — input renaming (`bind: {tag_name: version}` wires upstream output `version` to input `tag_name`)
- **`outputs:`** on `run:` steps — manual output annotation for untyped steps

```yaml
name: Python CI
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '${{ config.python_version }}'
      - run: pytest

  publish:
    needs: [test]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: bump
        uses: i2mint/isee/actions/bump-version-number@master
      - uses: i2mint/wads/actions/git-tag@master
        bind:
          tag_name: version  # wire bump's "version" output to git-tag's "tag_name" input
```

# reci.action_spec

Action contract model — parsed from `action.yml` metadata.

An [`ActionSpec`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.ActionSpec) captures the typed input/output contract of a GitHub
Action so that downstream modules (graph, compiler, validation) can reason
about data flow without fetching YAML at every step.

### Functions

| [`action_local_name`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.action_local_name)(ref)                       | Extract the last path segment of an action ref, normalized.                                                        |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`action_spec_from_declaration`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.action_spec_from_declaration)(ref, \*[, ...]) | Build an [`ActionSpec`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.ActionSpec) from inline recipe declarations.              |
| [`action_spec_from_ref`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.action_spec_from_ref)(ref)                    | Fetch action.yml from GitHub and return an [`ActionSpec`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.ActionSpec).            |
| [`fetch_action_yml`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.fetch_action_yml)(ref)                        | Fetch and parse an `action.yml` from GitHub.                                                                       |
| [`normalize_name`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.normalize_name)(name)                         | Canonical form: lowercase, hyphens/spaces → underscores.                                                           |
| [`parse_action_spec`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.parse_action_spec)(ref, \*, action_yml_data)  | Build an [`ActionSpec`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.ActionSpec) from a ref string and parsed action.yml data. |

# _autosummary/reci.compiler.html.md

# reci.compiler

Compiler — recipe + action specs + config → GitHub Actions workflow YAML.

The compiler resolves data-flow wiring using a five-level precedence, injects
a `setup` job that exports config values as job outputs, auto-generates the
cross-job output forwarding ceremony, and adds `needs:` edges from data-flow
dependencies.

### Functions

| [`compile_recipe`](_autosummary/reci.compiler.html.md#reci.compiler.compile_recipe)(recipe, action_specs, \*[, config])   | Compile a recipe into a GitHub Actions workflow dict.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|

### Exceptions

| [`CompilationError`](_autosummary/reci.compiler.html.md#reci.compiler.CompilationError)   | Raised when compilation fails.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|

### *exception* reci.compiler.CompilationError

Bases: [`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#Exception)

Raised when compilation fails.

### reci.compiler.compile_recipe(recipe, action_specs, , config=None)

Compile a recipe into a GitHub Actions workflow dict.

* **Parameters:**
  * **recipe** ([`Recipe`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.Recipe)) – Parsed recipe.
  * **action_specs** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`ActionSpec`](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.ActionSpec)]) – Action specs keyed by ref string.
  * **config** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Flat config dict (optional).  If non-empty, a `setup` job is
    injected, jobs depend on it, and config references are wired.
    Cross-job data-flow wiring happens either way.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/reci.config.html.md

# reci.config

Config resolution — flat dict with scoped overrides.

Resolution order for input `root_dir` of action `run-tests`:

```default
1. ``run_tests__root_dir`` in config → scoped override wins
2. ``root_dir`` in config → shared default
3. ``default`` from action.yml → action default
4. If required and none found → validation error (FLOW001)
```

### Functions

| [`collect_required_config_keys`](_autosummary/reci.config.html.md#reci.config.collect_required_config_keys)(recipe, ...)         | Scan a recipe and return config keys needed by its actions.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`flatten_config`](_autosummary/reci.config.html.md#reci.config.flatten_config)(nested, \*[, prefix])              | Convert a nested dict to a flat dict with `__` separators.    |
| [`resolve_config_for_input`](_autosummary/reci.config.html.md#reci.config.resolve_config_for_input)(input_name, ref, config) | Find a config value for an action input.                      |

### reci.config.collect_required_config_keys(recipe, action_specs)

Scan a recipe and return config keys needed by its actions.

Returns `{key: required}` where *required* is True when the input
has `required=True` and no default.  Inputs given by an explicit
`with:` or fed by an upstream step output (`bind:` honoured) need no
config key.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]

# _autosummary/reci.graph.html.md

# reci.graph

Recipe DAG — computational graph built on [`graphlib`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/graphlib.html#module-graphlib).

[`RecipeGraph`](_autosummary/reci.graph.html.md#reci.graph.RecipeGraph) wraps [`graphlib.TopologicalSorter`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/graphlib.html#graphlib.TopologicalSorter) to model
the two-level structure of GitHub Actions workflows: jobs containing
sequential steps, with inter-job parallelism governed by `needs:`
edges and data-flow dependencies.

### Classes

| [`ActionNode`](_autosummary/reci.graph.html.md#reci.graph.ActionNode)(step_id, job[, ref, action_spec, ...])   | A single step in the recipe graph.              |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| [`CrossJobEdge`](_autosummary/reci.graph.html.md#reci.graph.CrossJobEdge)(source_job, source_step_id, ...)       | Data-flow edge between steps in different jobs. |
| [`RecipeGraph`](_autosummary/reci.graph.html.md#reci.graph.RecipeGraph)()                                       | The computational DAG of a recipe.              |

### *class* reci.graph.ActionNode(step_id, job, ref=None, action_spec=None, with_=<factory>, bind=<factory>, if_=None, declared_outputs=<factory>, run=None, name=None, env=<factory>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A single step in the recipe graph.

Uses `step_id` + `job` as its identity (the graph keys these as
`"{job}.{step_id}"` strings for `TopologicalSorter`).

#### *property* input_specs *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [InputSpec](_autosummary/reci.action_spec.html.md#reci.action_spec.InputSpec)]*

steps.

* **Type:**
  Input specs from the action, or empty for run

#### *property* output_names *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]*

All normalized output names this node produces.

#### *property* output_spellings *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]*

`{normalized output name: spelling to emit}` for this node.

Declared (recipe) outputs come first; the action’s own `action.yml`
spelling wins when both name the same output.

### *class* reci.graph.CrossJobEdge(source_job, source_step_id, source_output, target_job, target_step_id, target_input)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Data-flow edge between steps in different jobs.

### *class* reci.graph.RecipeGraph

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The computational DAG of a recipe.

Nodes are identified by `"{job}.{step_id}"` strings.  The actual
[`ActionNode`](_autosummary/reci.graph.html.md#reci.graph.ActionNode) objects are stored in `_nodes`.

#### execution_waves()

Return parallel execution waves (topological generations).

Each wave is a tuple of node keys that can execute concurrently.
Raises `CycleError` if the graph has cycles.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]]

#### *classmethod* from_recipe(recipe, action_specs)

Build a graph from a parsed recipe and fetched action specs.

*action_specs* is keyed by action ref (e.g. `"actions/checkout@v4"`).

* **Return type:**
  [`RecipeGraph`](_autosummary/reci.graph.html.md#reci.graph.RecipeGraph)

#### upstream_output_names(node, , other_jobs=True)

Normalized output names *node* can be fed from.

Outputs of earlier steps in its own job, plus (unless *other_jobs* is
false) outputs of any step in another job, which the compiler forwards
through `needs`.

* **Return type:**
  [`set`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#set)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### validate(config=None)

Run all validation rules and return a ValidationReport.

Imported lazily to avoid circular imports (validation depends on graph).

# _autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md

# reci.recipe

Recipe model — declarative CI pipeline description.

A recipe is a YAML file that looks like a GitHub Actions workflow but with
reci extensions: `${{ config.* }}` references, `bind:` mappings for
input renaming, and `outputs:` annotations on `run:` steps.

### Functions

| [`parse_recipe`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.parse_recipe)(path)        | Load a recipe YAML and return a [`Recipe`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.Recipe).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`parse_recipe_string`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.parse_recipe_string)(text) | Parse a recipe from a YAML string (useful for testing).                                    |

### Classes

| [`JobSpec`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.JobSpec)(id[, steps, needs, if_, runs_on, ...])   | One job inside a recipe.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| [`Recipe`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.Recipe)(name, on[, jobs, env, defaults])          | A complete reci recipe.    |
| [`StepSpec`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.StepSpec)(id[, uses, run, with_, if_, name, ...]) | One step inside a job.     |

### Exceptions

| [`RecipeParseError`](_autosummary/reci.recipe.html.md#reci.recipe.RecipeParseError)   | Raised when a recipe YAML is structurally invalid.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/reci.validation.report.html.md#reci.validation.report.Finding)]

### reci.validation.rules.flow.check_unused_outputs(graph, config)

An output is declared but never consumed downstream.

Consumed means: matched by an input of a later step (by name, honouring
`bind:`), or referenced explicitly as `steps.<id>.outputs.<name>` (same
job) in a step’s `with:`, `env:`, `run:` or `if:`.  `needs.` references
are not counted: a recipe cannot declare job outputs, so only the compiler’s
own forwarding makes them resolve.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/reci.validation.report.html.md#reci.validation.report.Finding)]

# _autosummary/reci.yaml_gen.html.md

# reci.yaml_gen

YAML I/O wrapper using ruamel.yaml (YAML 1.2).

Handles the critical `on:` key (PyYAML treats it as boolean True),
wraps `${{ }}` expressions in SingleQuotedScalarString, and uses
LiteralScalarString for multiline `run:` blocks.

### Functions

| [`dump_workflow`](_autosummary/reci.yaml_gen.html.md#reci.yaml_gen.dump_workflow)(workflow, \*[, stream])   | Serialize a workflow dict to GitHub Actions YAML.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| [`load_yaml`](_autosummary/reci.yaml_gen.html.md#reci.yaml_gen.load_yaml)(path)                         | Load a YAML file and return a plain dict.           |
| [`load_yaml_string`](_autosummary/reci.yaml_gen.html.md#reci.yaml_gen.load_yaml_string)(text)                  | Load YAML from a string and return a plain dict.    |

### reci.yaml_gen.dump_workflow(workflow, , stream=None)

Serialize a workflow dict to GitHub Actions YAML.

If *stream* is `None`, returns the YAML string.  Otherwise writes to
*stream* and returns `None`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### reci.yaml_gen.load_yaml(path)

Load a YAML file and return a plain dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### reci.yaml_gen.load_yaml_string(text)

Load YAML from a string and return a plain dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# ai-agents.html.md

# For AI agents

`reci` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `ci-advisor`

Discuss and plan what CI/CD actions, jobs, and recipes make sense for a project. Use this skill when the user wants to talk through their CI strategy, asks “what CI actions should I use”, “what recipes make sense for this project”, “help me plan my CI pipeline”, “what should my CI do”, or wants advice on testing, linting, publishing, deployment, or code quality automation. Also trigger when the user asks about specific GitHub Actions, CI best practices, or trade-offs between different CI approaches — even if they haven’t mentioned reci yet.

```bash
gh skill install i2mint/reci ci-advisor --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`reci/data/skills/ci-advisor`](https://github.com/i2mint/reci/tree/HEAD/reci/data/skills/ci-advisor) (bundled with the pip package).

### `ci-migrate`

Migrate an existing GitHub Actions workflow to a reci recipe. Use this skill when the user wants to convert their current CI workflow to reci, says things like “migrate my CI to reci”, “convert my workflow to a recipe”, “refactor my GitHub Actions”, or “I want to use reci for my existing CI”. Also trigger when the user has an existing .github/workflows/ directory and asks about reci — they probably want a migration, not a fresh setup.

```bash
gh skill install i2mint/reci ci-migrate --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`reci/data/skills/ci-migrate`](https://github.com/i2mint/reci/tree/HEAD/reci/data/skills/ci-migrate) (bundled with the pip package).

### `ci-setup`

Create a new CI/CD pipeline for a project using reci recipes. Use this skill whenever the user wants to set up CI, create a GitHub Actions workflow, add continuous integration to their project, or says things like “make a CI setup for me”, “set up CI”, “add CI/CD”, “create a workflow”, or “I need GitHub Actions for this project”. Also trigger when the user asks about setting up testing, linting, publishing, or deployment pipelines — even if they don’t mention “reci” or “CI” explicitly.

```bash
gh skill install i2mint/reci ci-setup --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`reci/data/skills/ci-setup`](https://github.com/i2mint/reci/tree/HEAD/reci/data/skills/ci-setup) (bundled with the pip package).

### `reci-dev`

Guide for contributing to the reci codebase. Use this skill when the user wants to add features, fix bugs, add validation rules, add config adapters, or understand reci’s architecture. Trigger when the user says things like “I want to add a rule”, “how does the compiler work”, “I want to contribute to reci”, or asks about reci internals.

```bash
gh skill install i2mint/reci reci-dev --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`reci/data/skills/reci-dev`](https://github.com/i2mint/reci/tree/HEAD/reci/data/skills/reci-dev) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install reci`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/i2mint/reci/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://i2mint.github.io/reci/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`reci.md`](https://i2mint.github.io/reci/reci.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://i2mint.github.io/reci/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
